The systems in place for safeguarding voluntary patients in respect of leave and recording the decisions was inadequate and decisions were largely communicated by word of mouth which led to differences of understanding what had been agreed, the basis on which it had been agreed and by whom it was agreed. The system for monitoring leave was inadequate, reliance being placed on hourly checks. Consideration was not given to the appropriate amount of leeway to be given to the patient before escalating the fact of them not having returned, with patients being given 30 minutes or more
